summary: The root وصي (w-ṣ-y) primarily means to enjoin, command, or make a will. It involves giving a charge or instruction, often with a sense of care or guardianship.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: and He enjoined him; charged him; bade him; ordered him: (K, &c.:) he commanded him, بِكَ َا, to do such a thing. (Msb.)
أَوْصَى لَهُ بِالثُّلُثِ He bequeathed to him the third of the property. (MA.) أَوْصَى He made his will. See 2.
They enjoined, charged, bade, ordered, or commanded, one another. See an ex. voce تَبَاعَثُوا.
A person commissioned; a commissioned agent: (K:) an executor appointed by a will.

An injunction, a charge, bidding, order, or command: (K:) an admonition, with an endeavour to persuade: and a command: its place may be supplied by any word in which is the meaning of أَمْرٌ. (Msb.) And A will, or testament. (K, * TA.)

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
mentions_note: Forms Lane discusses inside another entry rather than defining as a headword. Values index into headwords[].
